encouragement: Your setup is solid and repeatable, and your backswing and top positions are largely close to where we want them — that’s a great foundation to build from. With a few simple drills to move your weight onto the front foot and finish your hips through the shot, you’ll get more consistent contact and more power.

top_3_takeaways.title: Shift weight to front
top_3_takeaways.feel_cue: Feel like you’re stepping toward the target so most of your weight is on your front leg at impact — imagine landing softly on that front foot.
top_3_takeaways.simple_drill: Do the step-through drill: make controlled half‑swings and after contact lift or step forward with your back foot so you finish with most weight on the front foot, repeating until it feels natural.

top_3_takeaways.title: Turn hips all the way
top_3_takeaways.feel_cue: Feel your belt buckle and back pocket turning to point at the target and keep turning through the shot instead of stopping right after impact.
top_3_takeaways.simple_drill: Practice no‑ball full swings where you focus on rotating your hips through to a balanced finish with the belt buckle facing the target, repeating until you can hold that finish.

top_3_takeaways.title: Start hips before hands
top_3_takeaways.feel_cue: Feel a small, deliberate hip turn that leads the downswing — like your lower body gently pulls the rest of you through while your arms stay relaxed.
top_3_takeaways.simple_drill: From the top, make slow‑motion swings where you pause and then begin the downswing by turning your hips toward the target a split second before your hands and club follow.

one_sentence_summary: Good setup and backswing, but you tend to hang back through impact and not fully turn your hips — practice stepping through to the front foot and finishing with your belt buckle to the target.
